headline: Leverkusen's five wins in Crete, and OFI's Hoffenheim warning
summary: Leverkusen come to Crete on a run of five straight wins, with 14 goals scored in those matches, and the market makes them 77.8% favourites against OFI's 8.6%. The home side have lost their last three and conceded 11 goals in five, so the gap looks wide. But OFI beat Hoffenheim 2-0 here in September, and that is why the handicap gives them a two-goal head start rather than more. The goals line sits at 3.5, with over and under split at 50%.
read: Leverkusen are clear favourites in Crete after five straight wins and 14 goals, while OFI come in off three consecutive defeats and barely created a chance in either of their European and derby losses. The one thing keeping this interesting is OFI's 2-0 home win over Hoffenheim — the market rates Leverkusen about two goals better and splits the 3.5-goal line straight down the middle.

facts.fact: Leverkusen are 77.8% favourites to win at OFI, more than nine times the home side's 8.6%.
facts.meaning: The market treats this as one of the widest mismatches on the card, not a close away trip.

facts.fact: Leverkusen have won their last five matches in all competitions, scoring 14 goals and conceding four.
facts.meaning: They come to Greece in rhythm, not managing a wobble — the run is the reason for the price.

facts.fact: OFI have lost their last three: 1-2 at Rennes, 0-3 at AEK Athens and 3-4 at Kalamata on Sunday.
facts.meaning: They have conceded 11 goals in five games and arrive on the back of a seven-goal defeat.

facts.fact: OFI have already beaten a Bundesliga side in this competition, stunning Hoffenheim 2-0 at home.
facts.meaning: It is their only win in five and the reason this is not treated as a formality for Leverkusen.

facts.fact: Leverkusen's 4-0 win at Lech Poznan came with 5.22 xG created and 0.57 allowed.
facts.meaning: Their Europa League form is built on volume of chances, not just finishing — they can overwhelm a defence.

facts.fact: OFI created just 0.12 xG in their 1-2 defeat at Rennes, and 0.21 in the 0-3 at AEK.
facts.meaning: Against organised opposition they have barely produced a chance, which is the worry against Leverkusen.

facts.fact: Leverkusen are without striker C. Kofane, who has three goals in six appearances this season.
facts.meaning: They lose a squad forward who has been finding the net, but the run has been built across the whole front line.

facts.fact: Victor Boniface, who has played 12 minutes this season, was left out of Leverkusen's Europa League squad for the Greece trip, with Jonas Hofmann picked as Martin Terrier's replacement.
facts.meaning: A squad-list call rather than a first XI blow — the forward line still travels strong.

sources.fact: Bayer Leverkusen are on a five-game winning streak in all competitions going into the OFI match.
Patrik Schick's scoring streak helped Leverkusen beat Freiburg and extend their run to a fifth straight win, moving them within a point of the Bundesliga summit.
After Martin Terrier's injury, Leverkusen chose Jonas Hofmann as his replacement in the Europa League squad, leaving Victor Boniface out of the squad for the OFI trip.
Victor Boniface has been left out of Leverkusen's Europa League squad for the trip to Greece.
Leverkusen's winning mood is described as spilling off the pitch, with a playful locker-room culture highlighted after the Freiburg victory.
OFI have already beaten a Bundesliga side, having stunned Hoffenheim 2-0.
Rennes beat OFI Crete 2-1 in the Europa League, coming from behind after trailing at half-time.
Rennes secured their first win of the European campaign against OFI Crete, having been behind at the break.
